_meta.source: Every point resolved individually against OpenStreetMap on 2026-07-30, including the individually mapped features on Île Royale and Île Saint-Joseph — the jetty, chapel, lighthouse, old hospital, bagne museum, children's cemetery and the réclusion compound. None is estimated. The map deliberately includes the mainland launch site, because the Guiana Space Centre's schedule is one of the two things that can close this call.

port_name: Îles du Salut (Devil's Island), French Guiana

port_pin.label: Débarcadère de l'Île Royale — the tender landing

bbox_hint.note: The three islands lie 11-14 km off Kourou. Île Royale is the largest and the only landing; Saint-Joseph is south-east of it; Île du Diable is north-east across a channel of roughly 200 m, and is closed to landing.

pois.name: Île Royale
pois.notes: 28 hectares, high point 66 m. The tender landing and the whole walkable day: prison blocks, hospital, chapel, warders' quarter, two cemeteries and a museum in the former director's house.

pois.name: Île du Diable (Devil's Island)
pois.notes: 14 hectares. LANDING PROHIBITED — CNES states it remains closed because of sea conditions, and there is no usable jetty. Dreyfus was its sole prisoner for 1,517 days; his hut has been a listed monument since 1987. Seen from Royale across about 200 m.

pois.name: Île Saint-Joseph
pois.notes: 20 hectares. The solitary-confinement compound, its cell alleys now roofless, and the warders' cemetery. Reached by a small inter-island shuttle when the sea allows — cash only in euros, and no facilities of any kind on the island.

pois.name: Kourou
pois.notes: The mainland town and the European launch site, 11-14 km away. The islands sit under the launch corridor and are evacuated and closed for every eastward launch, under a ban that survives a postponement.

pois.name: Débarcadère de l'Île Royale
pois.notes: The jetty where the tender lands. Everything on the island is on foot from here.

pois.name: Chapelle de l'Île Royale
pois.notes: The penal colony's chapel, and one of the few interiors on the island still whole.

pois.name: Musée du bagne
pois.notes: The museum of the penal colony, in the former prison director's house. Worth the time before you walk the ruins rather than after.

pois.name: Ancien hôpital de l'Île Royale
pois.notes: The colony's hospital. Royale held the administration and the hospital; the mainland camps had neither.

pois.name: Phare de l'Île Royale
pois.notes: The lighthouse on the island's high ground, at the top of the ring path.

pois.name: Cimetière des enfants
pois.notes: The cemetery for the warders' children. The convicts were not buried on land at all.

pois.name: Camp de la réclusion
pois.notes: The solitary-confinement compound on Saint-Joseph — a gateway, then alleys of cells now roofless and open to the sky.

pois.name: Cimetière des enfants des surveillants
pois.notes: The cemetery on Île Saint-Joseph for the children of the prison staff.
